source.label: Axler–Bourdon–Ramey, Eq1.19: Laplacian product rule

items.statement: Canonical local form of Eq1.19: for a finite-dimensional real inner product space \(E\), including dimensions zero and one, a point \(x\in E\), and real functions \(f,g\) which are C² locally at \(x\), the actual Laplacian and Riesz gradients satisfy \(\Delta(fg)(x)=f(x)\Delta g(x)+2\langle\nabla f(x),\nabla g(x)\rangle+g(x)\Delta f(x)\). The book states the real product rule for C² functions on their open domain in its standing dimension \(n>1\); the displayed canonical form localizes at one point and makes the low-dimensional extension explicit. It asserts no harmonicity or integral value.
assumptions: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner product space, and \(x\in E\). No positive-dimension premise is required. The source book works in \(\mathbb R^n\), \(n>1\); the canonical coordinate-independent form explicitly includes dimensions zero and one.

\(f,g:E\to\mathbb R\) are twice continuously differentiable locally at \(x\). The book identity applies to C² functions on their open domain. Here the local germ is sufficient; the former compact-graph implementation required global C² functions on E.

\(\nabla\) is the actual Riesz gradient and \(\Delta\) is the actual Euclidean Laplacian defined from the canonical covariant tensor and second Fréchet derivative. Neither is defined by the identity being proved.

obligations.label: Multiply two locally C² real functions, then take the Laplacian.

assumption_deltas.source: Eq1.19: real C² observables on an open domain, under standing Euclidean n>1.
assumption_deltas.lean: ContDiffAt R2 for both observables at x on an arbitrary finite real Hilbert space, including dimensions0/1.
assumption_deltas.reason: The proof uses only the germ at x; orthonormal trace and Riesz gradients remove coordinate choices. Empty/singleton basis cases are retained. The book is not claimed to state these low-dimensional interfaces.

assumption_deltas.source: Prop1.18 multiplies 1-norm(x)^2 by norm(x-zeta)^(-n) away from the unit pole.
assumption_deltas.lean: The concrete literal quotient kernel consumer discharges local C² inside the unit ball; no global C²-at-the-pole premise is imposed.
assumption_deltas.reason: A consumer regularity discharge, not a proof of harmonicity or either Poisson value.
